title: feat: add xan, html-to-markdown and file to the computer shell
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Enables the optional `xan` (CSV), `html-to-markdown` and `file` command groups from `@cloudflare/computer`
- Tells agents the shell is emulated and to check flags with `<command> --help`
- Leaves out `yq`: it needs `node:process`, which the shell's Dynamic Worker lacks (also with `enable_nodejs_process_v2`)
- Leaves out `sqlite3`, `python`, `js-exec`: they need `node:worker_threads` (sqlite fix pending upstream, cloudflare/computer#144)
- Test runs each new command in workerd (17/17 pass)

gist.headline: A Bigger Shell Garden
gist.blurb: The computer shell grew three useful little tools: CSV wrangling with xan, HTML-to-Markdown conversion, and file inspection. Agents also get a polite reminder that this is an emulated shell: ask the tools what flags they speak before getting ambitious.
gist.summary: The computer MCP shell now enables @cloudflare/computer's optional xan CSV, html-to-markdown, and file command groups, with agent guidance to inspect supported flags via <command> --help in the emulated workerd environment.
gist.impact: Agents using computer MCP can now inspect files, transform HTML into Markdown, and work with CSV data directly in the shell; all 17 command tests pass in workerd.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the computer MCP as a cozy retro terminal garden: Polli, wearing a tiny mechanic tool belt, helps a cheerful CRT monitor robot sort a CSV spreadsheet, turn an HTML page into a Markdown scroll, and inspect a glowing file folder. Use small command labels such as “xan --help”, “html-to-markdown --help”, and “file --help” to convey that the emulated shell reveals its available flags; surround the workstation with code-plants and flowers.
